A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cancer-Myth study, retaining the original pilot, dataset and generation pipeline. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original physician evaluations of 25 CancerCare questions, model results on 585 Cancer-Myth questions, and annotation-agreement analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds model evaluations, mitigation experiments, a question-realism survey, and further annotation and error analyses.

M1.justification: The adversarial generation loop, generation prompts and balancing algorithm remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds GEPA optimization of precautionary prompts and a monitoring agent within MDAgents, providing bounded prompt and inference adaptations.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 150 physician-validated Cancer-Myth-NFP questions without false presuppositions, plus MedQA, PubMedQA, SymCat, Medbullets and Craft-MD. These introduce false-positive controls and broader medical task coverage beyond the retained CancerCare and Cancer-Myth evaluations.

E2.justification: The overall comparison expands from eight systems in v1 Figure 6 to seventeen in v2 Figure 5, adding GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-4-Sonnet and Gemma, Qwen and LLaMA variants. Table 1 adds GEPA and monitored-MDAgents comparisons. DeepSeek-R1 disappears from the category-wise comparison, although its overall results remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include GEPA training and validation with five examples per dataset for each of seven datasets, comparisons with precautionary monitoring, and a realism survey involving ten question pairs and ten NLP researchers. The original pilot protocol and PCS/PCR evaluation remain intact; these additions do not establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of mitigation-induced overcorrection and performance degradation on other medical tasks, a question-realism study, and physician-disagreement analysis. Appendix C also adds cross-model correct-answer overlap and universally successful/unsuccessful cases. The original category and generator-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds Gwet's AC1 for physician agreement, pairwise human scoring agreement, and significance reporting for the realism survey. Conversely, v1's two model-comparison p-values in Section 4.3 are removed. These are localized statistical-reporting changes; no repeated-run, seed or confidence-interval practice is added.

E6.justification: Shared overall scores remain unchanged, including Gemini-1.5-Pro's 27.2% PCR and GPT-4o's 5.8%. Added models change the leader to GPT-5 at 42.1% PCR and 0.19 PCS. New mitigation results include Gemini-2.5-Pro changing from 41 to 88 on Cancer-Myth and from 96 to 68 on NFP in v2 Table 1. New agreement, overlap and case findings further expand the results.

T1.justification: The PCS/PCR formulas and scoring definitions are unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2's additional agreement statistics do not introduce new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion expand the contribution from documenting false-presupposition failures to evaluating mitigation tradeoffs using NFP controls. They newly argue that prompting alone is unreliable because improved correction accompanies overcorrection and reduced medical-task performance. The headline correction ceiling changes from 30% to 43% with the expanded model comparison.

C2.justification: v2 develops an interpretation centered on overcautious mitigation, limited benefits from model aggregation, and the failure of model size alone to predict correction performance. Appendix C.1.3 also explicitly defends retaining ambiguous questions despite physician disagreement, adding a substantive qualification to dataset validity.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies two human annotations and their averaging/rounding rule for the existing 76-example validation, reports public-model sizes, and states GEPA training/validation sample counts. Existing generation templates and code/data links remain unchanged. Mitigation prompts and detailed testing procedures remain underspecified, including in Appendix C.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds substantive discussion of (QA)2, FRESHQA, Pregnant Questions and human-grounded adversarial benchmarking. Recognition of related medical work narrows the novelty claim from the first medical false-presupposition benchmark to the first specifically for cancer care. GEPA and additional model/dataset references further expand the research context.

P1.justification: v2 locally revises the abstract, introduction and discussion, adds Section 4.4 and an LLM-use disclosure, and reorganizes Appendix C. The six-section main structure and most existing prose remain stable. Appendix editing also introduces an unfinished sentence in B.6 and duplicated explanation in C.1.3.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the overall model chart, revises and relocates the category chart, adds mitigation and public-model tables, and expands the agreement table. The unchanged dataset-distribution figure moves to Appendix B. Figure 4 gains category percentages, while Figure 2 changes its score histogram from counts to percentages.

improvement.justification: NFP controls, cross-benchmark mitigation tests and added annotation validation improve the evaluation beyond v1's predominantly false-presupposition-only analysis. However, the introduction's Gemini mitigation claims of 80% correction and 41% false positives conflict with Table 1's 88% correction and implied 32% false positives, and mitigation protocols remain underspecified. The broader evaluation supports a useful net improvement, but these reporting weaknesses limit the gain in overall rigor.
